title: PCA 15 15 coconut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PCA 15 15 coconut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PCA 15 15 coconut is a coconut variety from PCA. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: PCA 15 15 is a registered coconut variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Co 26. PCA bred it. Its record notes 2.16 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Yield:** 2.16 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

Its average yield of 2.16 t copra/ha beats the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit coconut fields most often: [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot), [coconut cadang cadang](/diseases/cadang-cadang), [coconut leaf beetle (Brontispa)](/pests/coconut-leaf-beetle), [coconut rhinoceros beetle](/pests/coconut-rhinoceros-beetle), [coconut scale insect (cocolisap)](/pests/cocolisap). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of PCA 15 15 weighs about 1,290 g grams, and its shape is round (polar and equatorial). The edible part is 57.7 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is 12, bearing biennial. Each palm gave about 70.7 nuts a year in the records, with 230.5 grams of copra per nut.
Where and when to plant PCA 15 15 coconut

Talls live long and stand typhoons, dwarfs bear early and are easy to harvest, and hybrids between the two give the most copra. Pick by use: copra, buko, or both. Get seednuts from a PCA accredited source. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.
